default_creds.context: Canonical docker-compose / Helm quickstart creates the bootstrap admin via ADMIN_PASSWORD / SUPERSET_ADMIN_PASSWORD defaulting to 'admin'. Operator opt-in to change; frequently shipped as-is on internet-reachable boxes.

CVE-2023-27524: Superset <=2.0.1 ships default SECRET_KEY '\2\1thisismyscretkey\1\2\\e\\y\\y\\h'. Flask signs the session cookie with it; an attacker forges {"_user_id":1,"user_id":1} and walks past the login wall as admin. Newer builds refuse the default key on boot, but operators override and never rotate. Dump shows 847 hosts emitting Set-Cookie session payload {"_user_id":1,"user_id":1} (surface marker, forgeable on default-key cohort).

install_tell: git clone apache/superset && docker compose -f docker-compose-image-tag.yml up (gunicorn :8088 + Postgres metastore + Redis + Celery worker); production deploys reverse-proxy 8088 behind nginx on 80/443. Helm chart 'superset' on Apache repo. ADMIN_PASSWORD/admin and an unrotated SECRET_KEY are the recurring quickstart sins.

active_probe.false_positive_check: Title 'Superset' is FP-prone: brand squatters (Udio Superset, Red Digital - Superset, MSI Superset, Superset Solutions Inc) and html-hash-collision noise (cameras, gateways, Proxmox, anything-llm strings) all surface on title:"Superset". Confirm with the vendor-unique data-bootstrap blob (keys SUPERSET_WEBSERVER_TIMEOUT / SUPERSET_DASHBOARD_POSITION_DATA_LIMIT) OR the 'Apache Superset:' response-header version block, neither of which collides. AI-backend wiring (pgvector/qdrant/weaviate/milvus connection) is NOT passively observable: http.html:"embedding"/"llm" are FALSE POSITIVES (Superset's own dashboard UI copy + anything-llm hash-collision noise). AI-wiring confirmation requires a /api/v1/database/ 200-with-data read (RBAC-misconfig or forged session) reading connection display names + URIs -> verify-lane action, not a passive dork.

auth_evidence: PRIMARY SOURCE: Superset ships a Flask-AppBuilder login wall (AUTH_DB), so auth is ON by default. The exposure is the default SECRET_KEY '\2\1thisismyscretkey\1\2\\e\\y\\y\\h' present in superset/config.py through 2.0.1; Flask signs the session cookie with it, enabling forgery of {"_user_id":1,"user_id":1} = bootstrap admin (CVE-2023-27524). Later builds raise on the default key at boot but operators override and never rotate. LOCAL DUMP (2026, superset.json.gz, 2000 records / 1178 unique IPs): 1594 records carry the vendor-unique data-bootstrap FAB blob; 754 emit the 'Apache Superset:' Version header (5.0.0=128, 4.1.1=79, 4.1.2=74, ... 2.0.1=16, long tail to 0.20.6); 847 emit Set-Cookie session payload {"_user_id":1,"user_id":1} (forgeable on default-key cohort, opaque on rotated hosts); 735 carry canonical favicon hash 1582430156; 353 are anything-llm html-hash-collision noise (NOT AI-backend evidence). Auth-on-default but default-SECRET_KEY-forgeable => login-wall-default-on with a known signing-key bypass on the <=2.0.1 / override cohort.

User accounts + roles via FAB security API; forged-admin session = full read of all of the above
